title: Descending the exchange property through a universal homeomorphism
statement:
Let $S'\to S$ be finite, surjective and radicial, and let
$j:X\hookrightarrow Y$ be an open immersion of finite-type
$S$-schemes with a constructible finite sheaf $F$ on $X$.
Suppose the direct image after base change to $S'$ is bounded
constructible and its formation commutes with every further base
change from a Noetherian scheme. Then the same assertions hold over $S$.
The notation refers to the canonical exchange morphism.

proof.text: A finite surjective universally injective v is a universal homeomorphism; so are pY and pX by pullback. The source topological-invariance theorem gives inverse-image equivalences. Apply the mate-isomorphism theorem to derivedSquareUpperStarIso and the derived inverse/direct-image adjunctions: the canonical cover exchange is an isomorphism (cover_exchange_iso).

proof.text: Prove finite-stalk reflection for any surjective q. Above the image of an arbitrary geometric point choose a point z upstairs and take the separable closure of its residue field. Its composite geometric point has the same image downstairs. Geometric-stalk comparison and upperStarCompSheafFiberIso transport finite generation from the upstairs stalk to the original stalk. Combine this with the proved local-constancy reflection for universal homeomorphisms.

proof.text: Transport an upstairs finite stratification through the homeomorphism. Locally closed constructible subsets, the partition and disjointness are preserved. Construct actual immersed schemes for the image strata using vanishingIdeal, its subscheme, and an open restriction. For each stratum take the pullback upstairs. Its projection to the base is a universal homeomorphism, and its other projection has exactly the original stratum image. The immersion-independence lemma transfers finite local constancy to this pullback, and the preceding reflection descends it. Convert back to the project constructibility predicate. No comparison of reductions is needed.

Apply constructibility reflection in each degree. Transport hbounded through the canonical cover exchange to obtain global bounded constructibility of Rj_*F on Y, without assuming S Noetherian.

proof.text: Put F'=pX^*F. The single-complex/pullback comparison identifies single F' with LpX^*(single F). Naturality transports the assumed upstairs exchange to single F'. For every Noetherian test upstairs, pullback preserves bounded constructibility (boundedConstructible_leftDerivedUpperStar); the assumed exchange then transfers it to the tested direct image. Thus the full source HasConstructibleDirectImageBaseChangeOn predicate holds upstairs. Apply the already stated finite-radicial Noetherian-test descent theorem, and project its exchange clause for each arbitrary downstairs test. Combine with the separately proved global boundedness.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $S'\to S$ be finite, surjective and radicial, and let
$j:X\hookrightarrow Y$ be an open immersion of finite-type
$S$-schemes with a constructible finite sheaf $F$ on $X$.
Suppose the direct image after base change to $S'$ is bounded
constructible and its formation commutes with every further base
change from a Noetherian scheme. Then the same assertions hold over $S$.

proof.text:
By [thm-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-invariance], pullback
by a universal homeomorphism is an exact equivalence of etale
topoi. It preserves constructibility in both directions: the
underlying spaces are homeomorphic, and finite locally constant
sheaves correspond on every stratum under that equivalence.
The equivalence intertwines the direct-image functor for $j$
with the corresponding functor for its pullback, including their
derived functors. Therefore it detects boundedness and
constructibility of $Rj_*F$.
For any Noetherian $T$ and morphism $T\to S$, the pullback $T'=T\times_SS'\to T$
is again a universal homeomorphism by
[lem-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-base-change].
Pull back the proposed exchange morphism to $Y_{T'}$.
Compatibility of exchange with composition in
[sbc-lem-base-change-composition] identifies it, through the
same equivalences, with the exchange over $S'$, which is an
isomorphism by hypothesis. The pullback equivalence is
conservative, so the original exchange is an isomorphism.
